# `>` — Sort down / Greater

Function. Hanzi: `大`. Ranks: `∞` monadic, `0 0` dyadic

`>Y` sorts the major cells of `Y` descending, as `[⍒Y]⌷Y` does. Ties keep their order.

```bpl
>30 10 20           ⍝ 30 20 10
>"b" "a" "c"        ⍝ "c" "b" "a"
```

`X>Y` tests X > Y for reals, and for characters by code point. A number is less than any character, as [`⍋`](delta-stile.qmd) orders them. Pervasive; tolerant.

```bpl
1 2 3>2            ⍝ $f $f $t
"abd">"abc"        ⍝ $f $f $t
'a'>3              ⍝ $t
```

See [`<`](less-than.qmd) to sort up, and [`⍒`](del-stile.qmd) for the indices that sort.

## Fast combinations

These trains and compositions give the result of applying their parts in turn, faster. [Trains](../evaluation.qmd#trains) says which spellings BPL recognises.

| Combination | Applies to | Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| `k↑> Y` or `(k↑)∘>` | a vector of reals or characters without keys, with the count at most a quarter of its length | selects the `k` largest items, or the `-k` smallest, without ordering the rest |
| `↑> Y`, `i⌷> Y` or `i⊃> Y` | the same vectors | selects the item of rank `i` from the top without ordering the rest |

```bpl
v←30 10 20 50 40 60 70 80 90 0
2↑> v                               ⍝ 90 80
↑> v                                ⍝ 90
(•explain "↑> v").fast.combination  ⍝ ["partial sort"]
```
